audit.whatIsWrong: Two things. First, the mirror's primary finding applies here in full: the page calls W a root in every trade instruction, when Rune Prison only slows unless Spell Flux is already on the target. Second, the early block names Zac's Q as 'Let's Bounce' — that is his R.
audit.why: Ryze's W text: it damages and slows, and roots only 'if the target has Flux on it'. So the ordering E-then-W is what makes every line on this page true. Zac's Q is Stretching Strikes (800 range, 14s at rank 1, auto-reset), W is Unstable Matter (350, 5s, percent max health), E is Elastic Slingshot (21s at rank 1), R is Let's Bounce! (120s at rank 1).
audit.corrected: Flux-before-W ordering written into the level-2 and level-3 phases and the wants; Q renamed to Stretching Strikes in the early block.

audit.whatIsWrong: This page gave Ryze all seven rows. The already-audited mirror resolved the same chart to Ryze, Skill, Zac, Zac, Ryze, Zac, Ryze.
audit.why: Restating the mirror rather than re-deriving it: Zac owns levels 3 through 5 and the first-item window on raw HP and percent-health damage; Ryze owns level 1, level 6 and two items. Four rows here disagreed with the opponent's page, which mirror-fix.js would overwrite anyway.
audit.corrected: win[1]/phases[1] -> Skill, win[2]/phases[2] -> Zac, win[3]/phases[3] -> Zac, win[5]/phases[5] -> Zac, with ratings inverted to match.

audit.whatIsWrong: Elastic Slingshot was the tracked spike with no cooldown, and one Do's line invented a 'fifteen-second invitation'.
audit.why: Elastic Slingshot is 21/18/15/12/9s — 21 seconds at rank 1, not fifteen. Unstable Matter is 5 seconds flat, which is why extended trades go badly.
audit.corrected: 21 seconds written into the level-3 phase and the Do's; Unstable Matter's 5-second percent-health clock written into levels 4-5.

audit.whatIsWrong: The page repeatedly says his blob passive out-sustains you, but never says which stat answers it, and treats his HP bar as something armour-and-HP itemization competes with.
audit.why: Cell Division heals him off shed chunks and revives him from bloblets; Unstable Matter deals a percentage of YOUR maximum health. Grievous Wounds is the buy that matters, and stacking health actively feeds his W.
audit.corrected: Grievous Wounds written into the first-item phase; percent-health warning written into the Don'ts and levels 4-5.

edits.before: Zac at level 1 is a melee without a meaningful gap-close — his Q (Let's Bounce) and W (Unstable Matter) are close-range, so you can Q-poke him freely as he walks up to last-hit. The threat starts at level 3 when Elastic Slingshot is online: that charge is telegraphed and interruptible, but if you are standing inside his cast range with W already spent, it lands and suddenly you are rooted and taking his full burst. Play level 1-2 to stack Manaflow and poke, and the moment you hit 3 you can start punishing — E the wave near him to apply Flux to both, W root him in place, empowered Q into the Flux cascade. His blob passive means he survives and regenerates, but you force him back and win the CS lead.
edits.after: Zac at level 1 has no gap-close — Stretching Strikes reaches 800 and Unstable Matter only 350, while Overload reaches 1000, so you poke from the tip as he walks up to last-hit. The threat starts at level 3 when Elastic Slingshot is online: the charge is telegraphed and it is only up every 21 seconds at rank 1, but if you are inside his range with your combo spent it lands and his burst follows. Play levels 1-2 to stack Manaflow and poke, and from 3 you can punish — E the wave near him to apply Flux to both, W to root the Fluxed target in place, then empowered Q into the cascade. Cell Division regrows whatever you shed, so win the CS lead rather than hunting the kill.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 become a resource war: Zac has no ranged harass so he cannot whittle you, but his Elastic Slingshot is now max-level and his all-in potential with jungle support is real. Treat Slingshot charge animation as a hard stop — if you see him lean back into the animation, W root him immediately to cancel it, or back off to break his angle. At 6 your Realm Warp adds a flank threat he cannot follow, and his own ultimate (Let's Bounce, the bouncing CC) is potent in narrow corridors — avoid letting him use the lane walls to maximize his bounce coverage against you. Keep the wave even or slightly pushed so you can dodge back toward tower on his Slingshot timing.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 become a resource war: Zac has no ranged harass, but Unstable Matter chews a percentage of your maximum health every five seconds and his all-in with jungle support is real. Treat the Slingshot wind-up as a hard stop — step out of the angle, and only expect a root to hold him if Spell Flux is already applied; a bare W just slows him. At 6 your Realm Warp adds a flank threat he cannot follow, and his ultimate Let's Bounce! is potent in narrow corridors, so never let him use the lane walls to widen his bounce coverage against you. Keep the wave even or slightly pushed so you can dodge back toward tower on his Slingshot timing.
